title: Employee dishonesty risks: losses and documents
excerpt: How a company in Moldova can distinguish accounting discrepancies, mistakes and potential loss without unsupported accusations or insurance payment promises.
imageAlt: Finance and warehouse staff neutrally reconciling records without personal employee information

seo.title: Employee fidelity risks in Moldova: records and assessment | ING Broker
seo.description: Prepare neutral facts, reconciliations, timelines and questions about possible insurance. An inventory difference alone proves neither fault nor entitlement to payment.

author: ING Broker editorial team
content:
An inventory difference or unusual payment does not alone prove dishonest conduct by an employee. For a company in the Republic of Moldova, assessment should distinguish an error, missing documents, a financial loss and any findings made by competent professionals or authorities. “Employee fidelity insurance” should not be used as a promise to recover every shortage.

This material explains how to organise administrative information about these risks. It does not establish guilt, provide methods for monitoring staff or confirm the availability of a product through ING Broker. Questions about individual rights, employment procedures and a specific incident require the appropriate legal and professional assistance.

Separate observation from accusation

“Two records differ” is an observation that can be checked. “An employee stole” is a conclusion with different consequences. In the initial record, identify the documents, the date the difference was noticed and the question that remains unanswered. Do not assume a cause. Do not publish people's names or investigation details in a commercial enquiry form.

The difference may require accounting reconciliation, a check of a goods receipt or a specialist's analysis. Keep the wording neutral until competent findings are available. An accurate file helps everyone involved understand what is known, what is being checked and which documents are missing, without turning an insurance assessment into an improvised investigation.

Which exposure does the company want assessed?

Describe the types of assets and processes concerned: goods, cash, payments or other relevant records. Do not publish current balances, access procedures, sensitive internal limits or detailed duties that could create vulnerabilities. For an initial discussion, general categories and administrative roles are enough, without personal names or access codes.

A business with physical stock has different documents from a company providing services and administering payments. Do not use a single description of “internal fraud” for every activity. Describe the risk in relation to what the business owns, what it manages for others and the obligations arising from its contracts.

Reconcile records before calculating the loss

For a discrepancy, retain the period concerned, the sources compared and any explanations already documented. An amount shown in a system may reflect an incomplete goods receipt, a duplicated transaction or a document entered later. This article does not prescribe an accounting method. It recommends keeping a result that the competent person can trace and verify.

Separate the estimated value of missing assets from verification costs and amounts recovered later. Do not present the same amount twice, as a stock shortage and an unpaid invoice, without explaining the relationship. For every total, record its source and verification status. An internal estimate is not automatically a loss accepted under an insurance contract.

The timeline may matter as much as the amount

Record when the transactions being examined took place, when the difference was noticed and which communications followed. These dates may differ. If the exact period has not been established, mark the interval as an estimate and retain the documents supporting it. Do not turn the date of a final report into the assumed date of the act.

For an insurance discussion, describe known circumstances openly. A new contract does not confirm acceptance of a situation already noticed. Ask about the contract period, discovery of the loss and notification by reference to the actual documents. Do not invent universal deadlines or retrospectively change the timeline.

Describe internal roles without unnecessary personal data

A preventive assessment can use categories of roles and approval principles without identifying individuals. There is no need to send a named list of all employees in an initial enquiry. For a specific situation, necessary information can be provided later through the agreed channel, respecting confidentiality and the directions of competent specialists.

Keep the discussion about prevention separate from questions of guilt. The absence of an internal control does not prove who caused a loss. Conversely, a written procedure alone does not show that it was followed or that an insurance product accepts the circumstances. Documents need to be read for the purpose they actually serve.

External fraud needs its own boundary

A false supplier message and dishonest internal conduct are not the same circumstance. For suspicious requests or disputed payments, involve competent institutions and specialists through known channels. This material does not recommend contacting the sender or provide investigation and technical access instructions.

Explain whether the alleged loss concerns internal action, a third party or an unknown cause. Do not force circumstances into a category because a policy bears that name. Cyber risks, professional liability and employee fidelity boundaries require actual wording checks.

Questions about a potential policy

Request definitions of the people, assets and acts to which the contract refers. Check the limit, deductible, territory and period. A deductible is the part of a loss borne by the insured under the contract. Ask about known situations, series of events and investigation costs. These are assessment questions, not guaranteed benefits or confirmed market availability.

Request notification procedures, documents and amount assessment methods. Do not assume an absent person, accounting difference or suspicion suffices for payment. The insurer examines contractual conditions, while competent processes establish facts and responsibilities.

Preserve records without improvised intervention

Do not alter records to make differences disappear or circulate employee information in open groups. Follow responsible professionals on document preservation and system access. This article provides no forensic collection, covert monitoring or personal-account access instructions.

An administrative file may list documents, responsible people and received requests. Keep identifiable copies and versions. Mark extracts and summaries so they are not confused with complete records or final professional findings.

Example: warehouse discrepancies

A business notices recorded stock differs from a physical check. The team records the difference and period, then requests competent reconciliation of incoming and outgoing documents. It does not publicly accuse an employee or automatically classify the shortage as insured damage.

This hypothetical scenario explains why receiving, transfers and records matter before conclusions. Once facts are clarified, insurance questions can include an explained timeline and value. The article does not decide intent, liability or entitlement in the example.

Preparing the company file preventively

Before incidents, prepare activities, value categories and general responsibilities. Summarise known history without unnecessary personal information. Show available procedures and external checks without claiming they eliminate risk or guarantee offer eligibility.

Identify people able to answer accounting, legal and operational questions. Do not automatically assign all roles to one person. “The document needs confirmation” can be more accurate than an approximate number presented as exact. Clarify outstanding differences before a definitive commercial statement.

Review after operational changes

New premises, collection methods or custody of customer assets can change exposure. Update administrative descriptions and records. Do not automatically transfer conclusions between sites where ownership or services differ. Review actual activities, not only the company name.

Insurance ING Broker SRL is a broker, not an investigative authority or the employer of people involved. The article confirms no product for every company. Availability, definitions and conditions require separate checks without recovery promises or unjustified staff accusations.

Customer property is not own stock

A warehouse or workshop may hold both its own goods and property belonging to customers. Identify the documents supporting that relationship and the time custody began, without publishing the contents of the files. A discrepancy involving customer property may raise different questions from a shortage in the company's own stock, including a possible separate claim.

Do not automatically add the value of the property to the amount demanded by the customer if they describe the same loss. Ask the accountant and legal adviser to explain the relevant documents. For insurance assessment, identify the category being examined and what remains unconfirmed, without declaring any person's guilt or claiming that the situation is covered.

Record changes may create apparent differences

Migration to a new system, introduction of a new category or transfers between stock records may require reconciliation. Keep the date of the change and the available documents. Do not conclude that every discrepancy during that period was caused by the system, but do not automatically describe it as dishonesty either. Competent people must be able to trace the sources.

In the administrative summary, mark which comparisons have been completed and what remains to be checked. A provisional amount may be revised when new documents become available. Keeping versions explains why the value changed instead of hiding the difference. For contractual assessment, this transparency is more useful than an apparently exact total that cannot be traced.

Frequently asked questions about employee fidelity

Does every inventory shortage prove dishonesty?

No. Competent people must assess and document the difference. Keep neutral observation, reconciliation, findings and possible insurance analysis separate.

Can a new policy be bought after discovery?

A new request does not confirm cover for a known situation. Present the exact timeline and request an answer against documents. Do not hide previous observations or communications.

Must every employee's details be supplied?

Not automatically in a first enquiry. Start with activities, roles and value categories. Necessary case information follows through agreed channels to relevant recipients.

Does insurance replace internal checks?

No. Records, professional assessment and contracts perform different roles. Neither an internal procedure nor a policy name guarantees absence or complete recovery of losses.
